correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=3 and b in [0,1], the graph symmetry average preserves the constraint and cannot increase centered spectral norm. The complete three-class quotient plus two internal eigenspaces yields exactly the four nontrivial eigenvalue values. Loewner monotonicity in the remaining edge weight proves the global lower bounds, with explicit attaining formulas in three regimes. The low and mid spectral dominance checks are exact factorizations; the high root uniquely balances alpha with -t_minus between a1 and b/m, where t_plus and beta are dominated. Endpoints and feasibility verified. The standalone checker reconstructed rational stochastic matrices/eigenvectors and tested 1313 exact identities and 334411 numerical alternatives; finite tests are supporting evidence only.

originality.rationale: Boyd et al. 2007 derive only unrestricted edge-transitive complete-bipartite FMMC (a single b=2/3 point). The proposed full fixed-single-vertex aggregate transition frontier has two nontrivial transitions at 1/(m+1) and 2/3 and a different high-throttle active mode. The literature of multipartite sensor graph topologies (2011) and clique lifts (2020) was materially inspected and does not state this fixed-row-aggregate constrained frontier. This is not a mere reparameterization of the recorded fixed-matching-edge constraint: fixed matching edges constrain m edges distributed among all rows, whereas the new condition fixes one row sum and leaves its individual entries free. No stronger/equivalent formula found; publication-priority risk remains.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently parameterized specialist literature may contain the same exact fixed-row frontier.
An inaccessible later version of a specialist manuscript could assert an unlocated equivalent formula.

value.rationale: A fixed outgoing probability at one designated node models a concrete local mixing/retention bottleneck. The complete all-size constrained SLEM frontier exhibits the natural saturation threshold 1/(m+1), a universal transition at 2/3, and an algebraic high-throttle active-eigenspace switch. The result is not a textbook substitution: it solves a global constrained spectral optimization, gives explicit optimal edge weights, and characterizes the changing binding modes for infinitely many graph sizes and all feasible throttle values.
